metadata.title: Meridian founder capacity reset
metadata.author: /root
metadata.author_note: Fresh verbatim-whitespace isolated replacement authored after the final behavior freeze. Each criterion is strict binary: award 1 only when every semantic conjunct in that criterion is satisfied, otherwise award 0.
metadata.presentation_note: Score meaning rather than headings or prose order, except for explicit branch precedence. There is no ceiling on supporting owners; one-primary-owner requirements apply only to the named job or decision domain.

prompt:
Today is July 15, 2026. Meridian Dispatch is a four-year-old, 14-person B2B software company founded by Leila Morgan and Omar Haddad. Its bank ledger shows $1.8 million of unrestricted cash. Signed recurring customer agreements provide $120,000 per month through June 2027, while payroll, founder salaries, taxes, infrastructure, rent, debt service, and every other fixed obligation total $100,000 per month over the same period. Every counterparty is current, and no cancellation, dispute, credit, offset, collection warning, financing need, or other company-survival concern is presented. HarborGrid’s migration must be completed by August 5 to avoid an interruption for its dispatch teams.

Leila and Omar have spent four consequential years working side by side: they closed the first six customers, built and operated the first two releases, handled two major outages, negotiated a painful refund, and led a layoff together. Leila currently owns sales, finance, and customer relationships and has a steady capacity of 46 hours per week for at least the next 18 months. She cannot work after 9 p.m. or overnight. Omar currently works 48 hours per week and owns engineering, delivery, deployments, and incident response. From October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027, he will be his father’s primary caregiver and can work at most 26 hours per week, Monday through Friday ending at 5:30 p.m.; he cannot work evenings, nights, or weekends and can no longer cover after-hours deployments or incidents. Neither founder has outside paid work, both depend on their current gross monthly salaries of $9,000 for Leila and $8,000 for Omar, and neither can put in more personal cash. Both still think the enterprise market merits at least another year: Leila is motivated by expanding customer use, and Omar by reducing costly manual operations. Neither is asking to leave, both would want an orderly handoff if they later did, and both say they are available now to negotiate reasonable minimum commitments and responsibilities.

Enterprise price exceptions, release sequencing, and senior hiring currently require both founders’ approval. A price exception, the HarborGrid migration sequence, and a support-lead hire have consequently sat for 18, 24, and 31 days. Leila remembers Omar agreeing on a June 27 planning call to own HarborGrid data validation; Omar remembers agreeing only to advise. The timestamped calendar invitation, an unreviewed call transcript, and the related Slack thread are retained, but neither founder has gone back through them. Northstar Assurance is scheduled to assess migration readiness on July 24, as shown by its July 11 confirmation, with a report due July 28. CloudRelay acknowledged Meridian’s July 12 request for an after-hours coverage quote and promised a reply by July 22; no price, scope, or service terms have arrived. Meridian’s three-person board consists of both founders and independent director Mara Singh. Elena Park is Meridian’s qualified current outside corporate counsel; she has not reviewed any possible operating or founder change.

How should Leila and Omar decide what to do next while keeping Meridian and HarborGrid covered? Give them a dated plan they can use.

criteria.description: PASS only if the response makes `partnership-primary` the sole primary route for the exact decision of whether and how this existing founder relationship continues under Omar’s prospective capacity and responsibility change, selects existing-team rather than candidate mode, does not open an ownership branch, and does not make company survival or time-to-zero a primary route on the supplied facts. Semantic equivalents for route and mode are accepted. Do not require or score any cash, receipt, obligation, or contribution figure; evidence classification; commitment-map content; current existing-team outcome; operating term; owner; date; future alternative; or safety/legal handling here.

PASS only if the response provides a finite evidence-status ledger for these non-commitment items: the bank balance, signed recurring receipts, fixed obligations, stalled-decision durations, the two conflicting June 27 recollections and retained calendar/transcript/Slack sources, the Northstar confirmation/assessment/report, and the CloudRelay request/acknowledgment/quote. It must assign each an observed, claimed, or unknown status or a clear semantic equivalent and preserve source/result splits: dated financial and operating records may be observed; each June 27 recollection remains attributed and disputed while the retained-source contents stay unknown until checked; the July 24 assessment existence/date are observed-as-scheduled while findings remain unknown through the July 28 report; and the quote request, acknowledgment, and promised July 22 date are observed while price, scope, and service terms remain unknown until received. It must treat the inconsistent recollection only as a concern to investigate, prescribe one narrow retained-source check with one named primary owner and due date, preserve a reversible option during that check, and make no inference about motive, deception, or harmful conduct. For this criterion the June 27 account is scored only as an attributed disputed past account and source-status question; do not score whether it describes a current or prospective responsibility or any other commitment-map field. Do not require or score either founder’s capacity, duration, outside work, personal constraint, salary or cash need, risk, responsibility, opportunity belief, motivation, exit expectation, willingness, selected route or outcome, or proposed operating term. No heading or presentation order is required.

PASS only if the response gives a complete finite map of the supplied founder commitments for each founder: current and future time and duration, outside work, personal constraints, salary and cash needs plus inability to add cash, risk, current and prospective responsibilities, opportunity belief, motivation, exit expectations, and present willingness to negotiate reasonable minimums. On these partnership-primary facts it must select exactly a prospective commitment-and-responsibility reset, or an unmistakable plain-language equivalent, as the current primary existing-team outcome because Omar’s future time and responsibility materially change; stalled decisions may support a relationship-repair subplan but not displace that primary outcome. It must expressly decline an optional new shared-work test solely because four years of consequential shared work already supply the needed evidence, and it must not recommend immediate founder exit or separation. Do not require or score the June 27 recollection or retained-source check, any response-proposed numeric minimum or operating allocation, an action date, a future replacement predicate, or safety/legal handling here.

PASS only if the response proposes current operating terms that remain conditional until Leila and Omar separately assent. The proposal must set a numeric weekly minimum for each founder within the supplied ceilings without requiring a restatement of those ceilings; use a bounded duration; respect Leila’s time-of-day limits and Omar’s time-of-day and day-of-week limits; assign every named decision domain exactly one primary owner while allowing consultation and escalation; define escalation, check-in cadence, a review date, reciprocal founder repair actions, and one named primary evidence owner for agreed behavioral and operating indicators. For HarborGrid, deployments, incidents, and after-hours gaps, it must name a current coverage owner through September 30 and set a dated acquisition-or-fallback decision for coverage after October 1; it may preserve an unknown vendor option but must not assume CloudRelay terms or invent provider availability. It must include a distinct observable operating indicator, such as a missed HarborGrid milestone or repeated decision latency, without requiring refusal or failure of founder minimums or a planned-exit consequence. It must not promise a permanent title, equity, or ownership change. Do not require or score supplied commitment facts, evidence-source statuses, the current branch selection, or any future replacement or safety predicate here.

PASS only if the response states four future replacement predicates with semantic precedence, without scoring or requiring the current outcome: first, an observed breach involving deception, exploitation, retaliation, concealed material obligations, or asset misuse overrides every softer predicate and leads to contained independently reviewed separation; second, refused or unavailable reset minimums or failure at a later founder-reset gate overrides repair or role adjustment and leads to planned exit; third, if commitments later align and truth and safety remain intact but a repairable interaction pattern becomes the main issue, relationship repair replaces the current branch; fourth, if commitments later align and an unsettled continuation-affecting founder role agreement is driven only by changed responsibilities, capability, or company needs, ordinary role reset replaces the current branch. Under the breach predicate, whether and when confrontation is safe must be owned only by Mara acting independently, an independent board committee, or qualified counsel. The response must preserve evidence, assets, access control, personal safety, customer continuity, and non-retaliation, and Elena or other qualified current counsel must own actual separation terms. It must not invent a clearance concerning conduct, access, safeguards, or continuity. Do not require or score routing, the evidence ledger or June 27 check, the current selected outcome, the commitment map, present operating terms, a current date or operating indicator, or a separate owner for each safeguard here.
